title: Local Radio News
description: Four short recordings from a local radio station: the news, the weather, an interview and a competition.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · The news
parts.intro: You will hear a news presenter on Riverside Radio.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: Good morning, and welcome to Riverside Radio news. I'm Nina Clarke.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: The town bridge will be closed for repairs from Monday until the end of the month. The council says the work was planned for the summer, but the bad weather in June made it start late.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: Drivers should use the old road through Millbrook instead. Buses will still run, but they will leave ten minutes earlier than usual.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: In happier news, the Saturday market is moving. From next week, it will be in the car park behind the library, not in the main square, because the square is being painted.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: And finally, a local boy, twelve-year-old Peter Hall, found a wallet in the park yesterday with two hundred pounds inside. He took it to the police, and the owner has now got it back.

parts.title: Part 2 · Weather and travel
parts.intro: You will hear the presenter talking to Dan, a reporter, about the weather and the roads.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: Now let's go to Dan for the weather and travel. Dan, what's it like out there?

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: Well, Nina, it's cloudy and quite cold at the moment, only about eight degrees. But don't worry, the rain from yesterday has stopped.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: So no umbrella today?

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: Actually, I'd take one anyway. It will be dry this morning, but there will be heavy rain after lunch, from about two o'clock, and it will stay wet until Thursday.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: Oh dear. What about the weekend?

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: Better news. Saturday will be sunny and warm, perfect for the market. Sunday could be windy, though.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: And the roads?

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: There's a long queue on Station Road because of an accident. A lorry hit a wall, but nobody was hurt. The police think the road will open again by eleven o'clock.

script.speaker: Nina
script.text: Thanks, Dan. So, if you're going to the station, leave early.

script.speaker: Dan
script.text: Or just walk! It's only fifteen minutes from the town centre.

parts.title: Part 3 · An interview
parts.intro: You will hear Tom interviewing Lan Pham about a new community garden.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: With me in the studio today is Lan Pham, who started the new community garden near the school. Lan, why did you start it?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Well, there was an empty piece of land behind the supermarket, and it was full of rubbish. I thought, why not make something beautiful there? Now forty people help.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: That's a lot! What do you grow?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Mostly vegetables, like tomatoes, carrots and beans. The children from the school planted the sunflowers. They love them. We tried strawberries, but the birds ate them all, so never again!

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Do you sell the food?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: No, no. Everyone takes some home for free. What's left, we give to the food bank. It's not about money, it's about being together.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: And what's the best part?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Honestly, meeting my neighbours. I lived here for ten years and I didn't know anybody. Now I have lots of friends.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: If someone wants to join, what should they do?

script.speaker: Lan
script.text: Just come on Sunday morning at ten. Bring gloves, and we'll give you a cup of tea.

parts.title: Part 4 · A competition
parts.intro: You will hear a radio announcement about a competition.

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Listeners, are you ready for a great prize? Riverside Radio is having a photo competition this month, and the theme is My Town. You can send us a photo of your favourite place. It could be a park, a shop or even an old tree.

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: To enter, send your photo by email, not by post. The address is on our website. Only one photo for each person, please.

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: The competition closes on the twentieth of May, and the winner will be announced on our Friday morning show.

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: The first prize is a weekend for two at the seaside, with two nights in a hotel. The second prize is a camera, and the third prize is a book of photos about our town.

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Remember, you don't need to be a photographer. Our judge, a teacher from the art school, says a good photo just tells a story. Good luck!
